title: Who Answers When It Goes Wrong? | Principles of Management Ep 25
description:
What happens when every small decision waits for the boss? Chai Corner now has five outlets and a small head office, but Meena still has to phone Ravi for every refund and every milk order. Ravi gets forty calls a day, and customers wait. In this animated lesson we use Ravi's chai chain to understand delegation of authority, step by step.

Ravi hands Meena a clipboard (the job) and a key (the power to decide). We time one refund before and after delegation, from twenty minutes down to one, then cover the three linked parts of delegation: responsibility, authority and accountability. You will see the key rule (authority moves down, responsibility is assigned and accepted, but accountability cannot be passed on), the principle of parity (authority must match responsibility), and what each idea looks like at work today, from a shift supervisor to a hotel receptionist and a buyer with a spending limit. We also look at the human side honestly: a 2015 Gallup study of 143 chief executives found strong delegators grew much faster, yet many managers still hold on out of fear, and work can creep back up, the famous monkey on your back from a 1974 Harvard Business Review article by William Oncken Jr. and Donald L. Wass.

This is Episode 25 of our Principles of Management series for MBA, BBA and commerce students.
